successors.note: "Jaipur's last princely ruler signed the accession to the Indian Union on 7 April 1949." The page names no Rajasthan union or date for the merger.

capitals.name: Amber (after Dausa and Khoh)
capitals.note: The page gives the sequence Dausa (first capital), Khoh, Amber, without years; the span is the whole period before Jaipur. Kakil "captured Amber from the Meenas and laid foundation of the future capital" (some sources credit Rajdeo).

capitals.name: Jaipur
capitals.note: "In 1727, He planned and founded a new capital city called Jaipur" (Sawai Jai Singh II); the page gives no day. The Jai Singh II page: he moved the capital in 1727, "construction ... began as early as 1725", and "by 1733, Jaipur officially replaced Amber".

rulers.name: Sawai Jai Singh II
rulers.note: "after the untimely death of his father Mirza Raja Bishan Singh on 31 December 1699"; died 1743 (21 September 1743 in the lead of the page). The page table of rulers on the Jaipur State page is partial and overlapping, so only this ruler is listed.

correction.text: the Kachwaha country of Dhundhar about Amber

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The page gives no extent or area for any date; a 60 km circle about Jaipur and Amber stands in for the Kachwaha country of Dhundhar (about 11,000 km2).

New keyframe: Dhundhar with Sambhar (captured 1708, jointly held); a 90 km circle (about 25,000 km2). No area or infobox figure on the page. The Jai Singh II page adds Shekhawati, Bundi and Rampura as acquisitions without a date and Malwa lost to the Marathas under the Treaty of Duraha (7 January 1738), but gives no extent, so the circle is unchanged; the Alwar State page gives 3,217 square miles (8,300 km2) for Alwar alone, a measure of how much the 1775 breakaway took.

minus.text: the eastern territory of Jaipur taken by the Jats of Bharatpur and the Kachwaha chief of Alwar

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Alwar State page says "He established the State of Alwar in 1775" and that Pratap Singh renounced his allegiance to Jaipur (undated); the Jaipur State page says "Late 18th century: the Jats of Bharatpur and the Kachwaha chief of Alwar broke away and each annexed part of Jaipur's eastern territory", sizes not given. The eastern band is removed from 1775 as one shape because the Jat share has no date of its own.

ledger.note: 1028: the Kachwahas migrate to Rajputana and take Dausa. The page says they "migrated to Rajputana in 1028 AD" and that Dausa was its first capital; infobox 1028-1949. The Meenas held Amber, which Kakil captured later (undated). The Kachwaha page opened gives James Mill's "migrated to Rajasthan in 1028 AD" and a citation to The Rajput Palaces that has the Kachwahas "founding Dhundar as their capital in 967 AD"; 1028 is kept as the Jaipur State infobox year.

1708: Jai Singh is restored at Amber and Sambhar is taken. "In 1708, Bahadur Shah invaded Marwar and captured the entire state. Amber was retaken by October 1708 and Jai Singh was restored"; Sambhar was "jointly ruled with allies after its capture in 1708". The counterpart is my reading (Sambhar was the Mughal faujdar's).

1727: Sawai Jai Singh II moves the capital from Amber to Jaipur. The Jai Singh II page: he moved the capital "from Amber to the newly established walled city of Jaipur in 1727"; "Construction of the new capital began as early as 1725"; "By 1733, Jaipur officially replaced Amber as the capital of the Kachawahas". The Jaipur State page: "In 1727, He planned and founded a new capital city called Jaipur."

region.text: the eastern territory of Jaipur taken by the Jats of Bharatpur and the Kachwaha chief of Alwar

ledger.note: 1775: Pratap Singh Naruka establishes Alwar State out of the eastern lands of Jaipur. The Alwar State page: "He established the State of Alwar in 1775"; Pratap "renounced his allegiance to Jaipur" (undated); he built a fort at Rajgarh "with Jaipur's permission" and took Swarup Singh's estates (undated). The page names no land with the date, so the band is my reading from the Jaipur State page ("Jaipur's eastern territory"); the share of Alwar against the Jats is not given, so the whole eastern band is carried here and in the next event. Alwar later joined the Matsya Union (18 March 1948); alwar-state has a dossier.

region.text: the eastern territory of Jaipur taken by the Jats of Bharatpur and the Kachwaha chief of Alwar

ledger.note: Late 18th century: bridging, page silent on the year. "The Jats of Bharatpur and the Kachwaha chief of Alwar broke away and each annexed part of Jaipur's eastern territory." Placed at 1775 beside the Alwar event because the two share one eastern band and the Jaipur page gives only "late 18th century"; the split of the lands between Bharatpur and Alwar is not given.

region.text: the Rajput country about Lalsot and Patan

ledger.note: 1787: Mahadaji Scindia's invasion of Jaipur. He "had to retreat after failure at the Battle of Lalsot" in 1787.

region.text: the Rajput country about Lalsot and Patan

ledger.note: 1790: the Marathas beat Jaipur at Patan. "He again invaded and defeated Jaipur army at the Battle of Patan in 1790" (20 June 1790 on the Gwalior State page). The page has further defeats at Fatehpur (1799) and at Malpura (1800) by Daulat Rao and Perron; the contest is not carried to those dates because the pages give no ground change.

ledger.note: 7 April 1949: Jaipur accedes to the Indian Union. "Jaipur's last princely ruler signed the accession to the Indian Union on 7 April 1949."

wars.name: Rajput campaigns of Mahadji Shinde
wars.outcome: Mahadaji Scindia was repelled at Lalsot (1787) and beat the Jaipur army at Patan (1790).

wars.name: Battle of Mandsaur
wars.outcome: Jai Singh II was defeated by the Marathas and had to pay chauth from 28 parganas; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Rebellion of the Rajputs against Bahadur Shah
wars.outcome: Amber was retaken by October 1708, Jai Singh restored and Sambhar taken and held jointly with Marwar.
wars.note: The page does not name the war; this is its entry for 1708.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary or area for any date; the shapes are circles about Jaipur.

sources.title: Jaipur State
sources.note: Kingdom of Amber and Jaipur: 1028 infobox, vassal statuses, 1727 Jaipur, 1708, 1732, 1787, 1790, late 18th-century losses to the Jats and Alwar, 1818, 7 April 1949.

sources.title: Alwar State
sources.note: Alwar established in 1775 by Pratap Singh Naruka, who renounced his allegiance to Jaipur (undated); East India Company alliance 1803; merged 18 March 1948 into the Matsya Union; area 3,217 square miles.

sources.title: Jai Singh II
sources.note: Accession after 31 December 1699; capital moved to Jaipur in 1727, officially replacing Amber by 1733; Malwa governorships; Treaty of Duraha 7 January 1738; died 1743; Shekhawati, Bundi and Rampura acquired undated.

sources.title: Kachwaha
sources.note: Migration to Rajasthan in 1028 (James Mill); an alternative founding of Dhundar in 967 (The Rajput Palaces); Man Singh as subahdar of Bihar 1587-1594 and Bengal 1595-1606; silent on extent.

notes: Four pages opened (Jaipur State, fetched twice for identity and for territory; then Alwar State, Jai Singh II and Kachwaha). The Jaipur State page is thin on territory: no area, no districts beyond the 1840 and 1854-55 reorganisations, no Shekhawati. Vassal statuses for the suzerains to record (infobox): tributary of the Chauhans 1071-1200; vassal of Mewar 1433-1527 (Bharmal met Akbar at Sanganer in 1562); vassal of the Mughal Empire 1562-1710; chauth to the Marathas from 1732; subsidiary alliance with the East India Company in 1818 (khiraj of eight lakh rupees; Jaipur Residency 1821); princely state of British India to 1947. The mughal-empire, british-empire and british-raj dossiers should carry the vassal_start/vassal_end events with counterpart jaipur-state. Rulers are not listed: the page's table is partial and overlaps. The 1780 year is a reading of "late 18th century". Counterparts needing dossiers: matsya-union; the Meenas (nobody). Three more pages opened: Alwar State (established 1775; used to date the eastern loss), Jai Singh II (accession after 31 December 1699; capital moved 1727, official by 1733; Shekhawati, Bundi and Rampura gained, undated; Malwa lost under the Treaty of Duraha, 7 January 1738; died 1743; silent on the Jats and Mandsaur) and Kachwaha (1028 against 967; silent on extent). Still undated and unplaced: Shekhawati, Bundi and Rampura gains, the Mughal-era Jaipur territory under Man Singh I and Mirza Raja Jai Singh I (only subahdar service in Bihar 1587-1594 and Bengal 1595-1606 is on the Kachwaha page), the Dausa/Amber/Khoh sequence, and the reorganisations of 1840 and 1854-55. The Alwar State page dates the Matsya Union merger to 18 March 1948 and the union's merger with Greater Rajasthan to 15 May 1949; the Jaipur page names no Rajasthan merger.
